subject: Regional capacity swap and onboarding plan for CelesteAI - US/APAC prioritization
messages:
From: Asha Mehta <asha@celesteai.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ops@celesteai.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pools for US + APAC ahead of Q4 launch

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the intro to Redwood at last week's AWS summit — CelesteAI is moving fast and we need to lock in inference capacity that maps to our Q4 product launch. Attached is a high-level traffic profile (celeste_traffic_profile.csv) that shows expected token volume and user concurrency by region. High level ask:

- US: target sustained ~200 A100-equivalent GPUs; ability to burst to ~500 for marketing-driven spikes.
- APAC (Singapore first): pilot committed 80-120 GPUs, burst to 300.
- EU: keep current baseline (~80 GPUs) but prefer not to grow right now.

Primary asks from our side: committed vs burst pricing, estimated lead time to have committed capacity in-region, whether Redwood can do a temporary pool reallocation (move spare EU capacity to US until APAC is standing) and what operational controls you provide for routing and fallback.

We'd like a pragmatic plan with timelines (pilot -> full commit), and a sample SOW so we can align procurement. Launch target is mid-November.

Appreciate a short call this week to walk the numbers.

Best,
Asha Mehta
Head of Infrastructure
CelesteAI

Attachment: celeste_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@celesteai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pools for US + APAC ahead of Q4 launch

Hi Asha — thanks, and congrats on the upcoming launch. We reviewed the CSV and this is helpful. Quick answers up front and a couple of clarifying asks so we size correctly:

1) Yes, we can support committed capacity per region plus burst lanes. Pricing delta for burst vs committed depends on reservation length and expected sustained utilization.
2) Temporary pool reallocation is possible but has constraints (lead time, SLA delta, and required internal approval).

Couple things we need to finalize your sizing:
- Peak RPS and expected concurrent sessions during marketing spikes
- Average and 95th percentile sequence lengths (tokens)
- Model family and typical prompt/response sequence (decoder vs encoder-decoder)
- Whether you need KV cache warmstart during cutover

Can we do a 30-minute call Thursday or Friday? Marissa (capacity/product ops) and Rachel (pricing/finance) are cc'd and will lead the sizing and SOW draft. I'll pull preliminary timelines and a swap-approach we can use if APAC isn't ready before US demand ramps.

I'll attach a short capacity questionnaire and our template SOW after internal alignment.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_capacity_questionnaire.pdf (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed regional sizing and swap plan for CelesteAI (draft)

Karthik / Rachel — drafting a short working proposal we can send to Asha once we agree. Key assumptions based on the traffic CSV and our follow-up Qs: 6-8ms token latency target for US, 10-12ms for APAC pilot, average request = 1.8k tokens (round trip), peak marketing spikes = ~2.5x baseline for 48-72 hour windows.

Proposed committed reservations (A100-equivalent):
- US committed: 220 GPUs (covers baseline + 20% buffer)
- APAC committed: 120 GPUs pilot (can scale to 200 committed in tranche 2)
- EU baseline: 80 GPUs (no change)

Burst configuration:
- US burst pool: additional 280 GPUs (burst lanes routed through pooled bursting; preemptible pricing)
- APAC burst pool: 180 GPUs

Pool-swap approach (minimizes risk and lead time):
1) Immediately reserve US committed at 50% delivered from our existing spare EU capacity (temporary routing + regional affinity). Estimated time: ~3 weeks to configure routing, KV warmstart plan required.
2) Begin APAC pilot provisioning (Singapore) in parallel — hardware ETA ~6 weeks for pilot nodes.
3) Full US capacity delivered over 7-8 weeks as procurement and physical allocation completes.

Tradeoffs / risks:
- Performance: temporary EU->US routing increases cross-region latency for affected EU traffic; we mitigate by keeping critical EU customers pinned to local nodes.
- SLA: temporary reallocation reduces redundancy in EU; need exec approval for reduced regional redundancy while swap in progress.
- Billing: committed vs burst pricing needs sign-off from finance for the upfront reservation term (12 vs 24 months materially changes unit price).

Action items before sending external:
- Confirm deal term preference (12 vs 24 months) and billing owner (Celeste procurement contact)
- Rachel to run pricing scenarios and impacts on ARR/TCV
- Karthik to confirm whether Celeste wants a DocuSign SOW or PO-first workflow

Attachments: capacity_model.xlsx, initial_sow_draft.docx

Marissa
Director, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@celesteai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated plan + SOW next steps (CelesteAI)

Hi Asha — appreciate the traffic file and the call earlier. We reviewed internally and attached a pragmatic plan and a draft SOW to get procurement moving. Summary:

- US: we can deliver ~110 (50%) of the requested committed capacity within ~3 weeks using a temporary reallocation approach; full committed 220 in ~7-8 weeks pending procurement sign-off.
- APAC (Singapore pilot): hardware provisioning begins immediately; pilot (120 committed) available in ~6 weeks, tranche 2 to 200 in another 4-6 weeks depending on capacity supply.
- EU: we will hold the current baseline (80) and only reallocate surplus nodes with your approval — we'll document any SLA reductions during swap.

Pricing / contract flow:
- We included two pricing scenarios in the attached SOW: 12-month and 24-month committed terms, with burst discounts called out for preemptible lanes. Rachel is available to walk the delta.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm deal term (12 vs 24 months) and procurement contact email.
2) We provision the 50% US committed as a short-term reallocation while procurement processes the full reservation (requires a signed short SOW / PO).
3) We open the DocuSign SOW (link below) for signature; once signed we'll start node provisioning and regional routing configuration.

DocuSign SOW link: https://www.docusign.com/ts/placeholder-sow-link
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4521
Attachments: capacity_model.xlsx, initial_sow_draft.docx

If that all sounds good, I can loop in finance/legal for final terms and get a PO/SOW sent today.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
